svg.title: NORTHSTAR study simplified data flow diagram with trust boundaries and STRIDE hotspots
svg.desc: Three sources (a hospital study site using REDCap, a biobank sample register, and NHS England Hospital Episode Statistics) each sit inside their own trust boundary and send data into a Trusted Research Environment through a single ingress step. Inside the environment the data passes in a straight line through linkage, provisioning, research and egress; an accredited researcher works inside and only checked outputs leave to publication. Nine STRIDE hotspots are marked.

text.tspan: NORTHSTAR study — where the data goes, and where the risk is
Simplified data flow diagram with trust boundaries and STRIDE hotspots · DASC513 week 6 · teaching example, fictional study
F3 study ID typed in by hand
TRUST BOUNDARY 4 · Trusted Research Environment (NHS Secure Data Environment)
no internet · no copy-paste · no removable media · everything logged
Hospital system auto-fills demographics: wrong patient, nobody notices
Study ID typed by hand onto the sample: transposed digits, no record
Identifiable export crosses a boundary: interception, wrong recipient
Linkage matches the wrong records, or misses the right ones
The ingress door accepts a file: fake sender, tampered file, flood
Linked data identifies people that separate files did not
Project gets more data than it was approved for
A disclosive table or model leaves the environment
Log incomplete or altered: nobody can prove what happened
S T R I D E = spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information
disclosure, denial of service, elevation of privilege
External entity — a person or system outside your control
Process — does something to the data
Data store — where data sits still
